Motivation

The reference data problem.

Every analysis starts the same way: somebody downloads a genome. Then somebody else downloads it again.

  • 01The same FASTA fetched five times across one shared filesystem.
  • 02Groups quietly running against different Ensembl releases.
  • 03“Where did this come from?” answered from someone’s bash_history.
  • 04A known-sites file that says chr1 beside a genome that says 1, and the analysis runs to the end anyway.
refdata-flow03 / 18

What we wanted

Five things, non-negotiable.

01
Reproducible
What the vault holds is fixed and identified. A new release is a new tag beside the old.
02
Zero duplication
One copy on disk, shared across users, requests and aliases.
03
Ergonomic
Ask for GRCh38 or mouse, not for a URL or a release number.
04
HPC-native
Resumable, parallel, conda-managed. The vault, not work/, is the record.
05
Auditable
A record for every asset, and the whole vault as an RO-Crate.

refdata-flow, in one sentence

What it is.

A Nextflow pipeline that turns a small CSV of species queries into a checked, versioned, refgenie-managed reference vault.

Input
CSV of queries
GRCh38 · mouse · sacCer3
Engine
Nextflow + genomepy
conda · resume · parallel
Output
refgenie vault
digest · aliases · RO-Crate
Consumed by
Paths from refgenie seek
rnaseq-flow · GATK · VEP

Architecture

Four stages, one run.

01 · Resolve
Generic queries to exact assemblies.
resolve.py · Python
Searches the providers you name, prompts on ambiguity, checks the rows, caches the answers.
02 · Fetch
Only what the vault lacks.
main.nf · genomepy
A preflight asks the vault first. One task per row, four at a time, retried.
03 · Register
Digest, aliases, record.
REGISTER · refgenie 0.13
Files each genome under its digest, adds a sequence dictionary, links every alias.
04 · Derive & check
What analyses need beside it.
gffread · UCSC · htslib
A transcriptome and small derived files; resources checked against their genome.
requests_resolved.csv
provider/species/assembly/
data/<digest>/ + alias/
fasta_txome · tx2gene · clinvar
refdata-flow07 / 18
01

Stage 1

Resolution.

From “GRCh38” to an exact assembly, before a byte is downloaded.

  • ↳Searches the providers you name. Ensembl, UCSC, NCBI or GENCODE; all four if you leave it blank.
  • ↳Interactive on ambiguity. Several matches for “mouse”? You pick once, and the choice is written down.
  • ↳Cached per query. Keyed on species, query and release, so editing a query re-resolves it.
  • ↳Checked before downloading. No annotation where none is published, no two rows for one download, no alias on two genomes.

requests/requests_raw.csv

# species,query,provider,annotation,aliases,release
Homo_sapiens,GRCh38,ensembl,true,human,116
Mus_musculus,mouse,ensembl,true,mm39;mm,
Saccharomyces_cerevisiae,sacCer3,ucsc,true,yeast,

Empty provider: search all four. A release pins Ensembl only.

refdata-flow08 / 18
02

Stage 2

Fetch.

Ask the vault first; download only what it lacks.

  • ↳Preflight against the vault. Each request is SKIP or FETCH, with the reason. Re-runs no longer depend on work/.
  • ↳Parallel, polite, retried. One task per row, four at a time; a failed download is tried twice more.
  • ↳Follows the provider. An unpinned row is fetched again when Ensembl publishes a newer release, and gains a tag.
  • ↳A record per download. provenance.json: source URLs, accession, SHA-256 of each file, counts, tool versions, UTC time.

the preflight, before anything downloads

Preflight: checking 3 request(s) against the vault
  SKIP   GRCh38.p14 from Ensembl, release 116:
         genome and ensembl_gtf:116 are in the vault
  SKIP   sacCer3 from UCSC: genome and
         ucsc_gtf:20210210 are in the vault,
         and 20210210 is current
  FETCH  GRCm39 from Ensembl: Ensembl now publishes
         ensembl_gtf release 117; the vault has 116
Preflight: 1 to download, 2 already in the vault.
refdata-flow09 / 18
03

Stage 3

Register.

Loose downloads become a content-addressed, alias-rich vault.

  • ↳Self-initialising. The first run creates refgenie_export.yaml.
  • ↳A digest per genome. refgenie hashes every record’s name, length and sequence, and files the genome under it.
  • ↳Named once, reachable by many. Always <assembly>_<provider>; your aliases link straight to it.
  • ↳Ready for GATK. A sequence dictionary beside every FASTA; each annotation tagged with its release.

what gets written

# content-addressed: the vault
data/89c2a7e1…/fasta/default/
    89c2a7e1….fa  .fa.fai  .dict  .chrom.sizes
data/89c2a7e1…/ensembl_gtf/116/
    89c2a7e1….gtf.gz
# readable: one link per file
alias/human/fasta/default/human.fa
alias/GRCh38_p14_ensembl/fasta/default/…
#   each straight to data/89c2a7e1…/
refdata-flow10 / 18
04

Stage 4

Derive.

The small files every pipeline asks for, made once from the vault’s own.

  • ↳A transcriptome, not a download. gffread cuts every transcript from the vault’s genome and GTF: lncRNAs included, contigs matched.
  • ↳Tagged with the annotation. fasta_txome:116 comes from ensembl_gtf:116; both are recorded as its parents.
  • ↳Checked, then registered. A .2bit is read back and must equal the genome, or nothing is registered.
  • ↳No aligner indexes. They depend on a tool version and k-mer choices, which belong to an analysis.

asset · what it is · read by

fasta_txome  transcripts     salmon, kallisto
tx2gene      tx → gene       tximport
gtf_indexed  sorted + .tbi   VEP --gtf, IGV
bed12        BED12           RSeQC
refflat      refFlat         Picard
twobit       .2bit           deepTools, BLAT
refdata-flow11 / 18

Beside the genome

Resources, checked against their genome.

  • ↳Asked for by name and build. clinvar:GRCh38 in the row’s resources column.
  • ↳Fetched only when new. The publisher is asked for its version on every run, a resumed one included.
  • ↳Checked before it is registered. Enough records on the genome’s sequences, none past a sequence’s end, lengths that agree.
  • ↳Renamed where it must be. dbSNP’s RefSeq names become the genome’s own, through NCBI’s assembly report.
ResourceBuildsFits
clinvarGRCh38, GRCh37Ensembl names
blacklisthg38, mm10, …UCSC names
GATK bundle ×6hg38the Broad genome
dbsnp b157GRCh38, GRCh37renamed to fit
vep_cachethe annotation’s releaseunpacked

No genome at all

Databases, filed beside the vault.

<outdir>/databases/
├── databases.tsv        # one line per version
├── swissprot/2026_04/
│   ├── uniprot_sprot.fasta.gz
│   └── provenance.json
├── pfam/39.0/
├── silva/138.2/
└── kraken2_viral/20241228/  # kraken2 --db
  • ↳Listed in a file of their own. requests/databases.csv: Swiss-Prot, Pfam, SILVA, Kraken 2.
  • ↳Versioned by the publisher. The release is read before anything is fetched; one already held is not fetched again.
  • ↳A new release is a new directory. Nothing is replaced, so an analysis can keep naming its version.
  • ↳Appears in one step. Staged out of sight, renamed into place, listed in databases.tsv and the RO-Crate.

From the user side

One command, end to end.

Edit a CSV, run the wrapper, point it at storage. Everything else is automatic.

typical run

# 1. genomes and resources: requests/requests_raw.csv
# 2. databases, if any: requests/databases.csv

bash run_pipeline.sh requests/requests_raw.csv \
     --outdir /reference_data/

# resolve → fetch → register → derive → check

useful flags

  • --dry-runResolve and report. Touch nothing.
  • --cleanupDrop downloads once verified in the vault.
  • --refetchDownload again, even what the vault holds.
  • --profile sgeSubmit the derivations as cluster jobs.
  • --cleanEmpty work/ and .nextflow/. Vault untouched.

What you end up with

Two halves: a vault, and human names.

/reference_data/
├── refgenie_export.yaml     # the index
├── ro-crate-metadata.json   # the vault, described
├── data/                    # by digest
│   └── 89c2a7e1…/
│       ├── fasta/default/      .fa .fai .dict
│       ├── ensembl_gtf/116/
│       ├── fasta_txome/116/
│       └── clinvar/20261109/
├── alias/                   # one link per file
│   ├── human/               → data/89c2a7e1…/
│   └── GRCh38_p14_ensembl/  → data/89c2a7e1…/
└── provenance/index.tsv     # the vault as a table
  • ↳The vault is the truth. Genomes filed by digest; bytes never move once written.
  • ↳Aliases are the doorway. Each links straight to the digest, one link per file, renamed: human.fa.
  • ↳The FASTA is uncompressed. refgenie decompresses it to index it; budget for that.
  • ↳Readable without refgenie. index.tsv and the RO-Crate list everything held.
refdata-flow15 / 18

On disk

Storage, by design.

01 — Fetched once
The vault decides.
The preflight skips what the vault holds, so losing work/ costs nothing already registered.
--refetch to force it
02 — Kept until verified
Nothing deleted by default.
Downloads stay. --cleanup removes one only after its FASTA and GTF are in the vault, its record copied out first.
--cleanup is opt-in
03 — Measured first
Room checked before fetching.
A fetch compares the announced size with free space. A large resource is held up to three times until work/ is cleaned.
--clean empties work/
refdata-flow16 / 18

Identity and audit

A digest for each genome. A record for each asset.

A digest, 89c2a7e1…, is computed from the sequences themselves: each record’s name, length and bases, in order. Not a filename. Not a URL. The sequences.

What it gives you
Same sequences, same digest. A different digest means different data.
What it does not claim
It covers the FASTA only, in refgenie’s own encoding: related to GA4GH refget, not conforming to it.
How it is audited
A provenance.json per asset, and the vault as an RO-Crate that passes the validator’s required checks.
